design: DESIGN §3.2.2 stint-level validation re-run over a prior-dynamics grid (owner review 2026-10-01: veterans looked too sticky). Two metrics per setting: (1) next-30-day weighted MSE of stint xG/60 at 7 as-of dates per season (the tuning objective, as shipped); (2) next-season: players fixed at the season-start prior mean (covariates fitted on the season), scored on every EV row of the season, which isolates the summer roll-forward
xg_source: xg_v2 walk-forward OOS (bu.rapm.v2_source); lake 2010-11..2025-26, burn-in 2010-11, cells recorded 2021-22..2025-26
decision: keep the current setting v0.02_k1.25 (q_add 0, aging_scale 1, young_old_extra 0.25). The tuning-best q_add 0.001 gains 0.0004 on the tuning 30-day MSE (z -0.65) but loses on the next-season metric (tuning +0.0008, dev +0.0007, 2025-26 +0.0038, z 3.9) and on the 2025-26 30-day MSE (+0.0021, z 1.8); the per-season stability check fails (2021-22 picks the current setting, 2022-23 k1_q0.004), so DESIGN §3.2 prefers the more regularised neighbour, which is the current setting. A stronger aging step (aging_scale 1.5/2.0) and wider age-tail variance (young_old_extra 1.0) are worse on every metric. The data do not support making veterans move faster. Game-level check of the tuning-best candidate: bu/lineup/out/lineup_eval_rapm_fin.json
